title: Geo cutover optimizer — adaptive tier routing and variant fallback validation
creator: Asha Patel
description: Deliver an end-to-end orchestrator that performs capacity-aware geo cutovers with adaptive tier routing and deterministic fallback to compatible model variants. The goal is a controlled multi-region handoff that minimizes user-facing latency spikes and token-cost regressions while ensuring cache priming and model-compatibility constraints are respected.
tasks: T1: Design probabilistic region scoring and weight decay algorithm (score = latencySLOCompliance * capacityHeadroom * healthFactor)
T2: Implement tier arbitration service that maps route tiers -> allowed regions and enforces per-region concurrency caps
T3: Add compatibility fingerprinting for fallback model variants (tokenizer/hash, kv-compat, sequence-limits)
T4: Prefill harness: synthetic shadow traffic generator with sequence-length distribution & KV prewarm probes
T5: Implement cutover executor: canary traffic shift, progressive step-up, automated backoff on latency/err-rise
T6: Integration test: simulate 30% regional capacity outage and validate cutover decisions and metrics
T7: Dashboard: per-route cutover scorecard + post-cutover regression alerts
T8: Docs & runbook: operational playbook for manual override and rollback commands
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Kickoff — aligned on success metrics with Product and SRE. Agreed to use existing runtime heartbeats + new capacityHeadroom metric.

2026-03-11: Completed design doc (link below). Chose probabilistic scoring to allow graceful weighting rather than binary gating. Decided to keep model-compat fingerprints minimal to speed runtime checks.
2026-03-12: Implemented tier arbitration prototype and basic score aggregator (alpha). End-to-end simulation harness started ingesting synthetic traffic profiles.
2026-03-13: First integration run: simulated partial region outage. Observed KV cache miss spike during step-up — added prewarm probes to task list.
2026-03-13: Open PR created for tier arbitration service (github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2197) — awaiting review from @maria-s and @jong.
decision_log: Use probabilistic scoring vs deterministic failover to reduce oscillation during transient noise (voted 4-1)
Limit automatic cutover to 'tier-locked' routes for first release; global default routes remain manual by PM approval
Fallback variants must pass a lightweight fingerprint compatibility check before being considered for routing
Throttle prewarm generators to avoid overloading warm standby region GPUs during large-scale cutovers
risks: Risk: Thundering herd on warm-standby warmup can overload capacity — mitigated by tokenized backoff and randomized ramp windows
Risk: Variant fallback may change output distribution (quality regression) — mitigate with small canary percentage and tied eval checks
Risk: Incorrect compatibility fingerprint could allow an incompatible variant — reduce surface area of fingerprint and add deterministic unit checks
Risk: Metric delay (30s Prom scraping) causing delayed decisions — SRE to expose lower-latency health probe for scoring
qa_plan: Unit tests for score computation with synthetic inputs and edge cases (all zero headroom, network flaps)
Integration tests: geo-sim v2 runs with adversarial traffic (spikes, long seqs, embeddings heavy)
Canary rollout in staging: enable automatic cutover for single test route, observe 99/95/50 latency, errors, token cost delta
Regression evals: run prompt-suite against primary and fallback variants and assert no regression > 2% on baseline metrics
acceptance_criteria: AC1: During a simulated regional outage (30% capacity loss) the orchestrator completes cutover within 60s for tier-locked routes
AC2: 99th percentile latency increase across affected routes <= 20% during cutover in integration sim
AC3: Fallback variant selection only chooses variants passing compatibility fingerprint and model-eval threshold
AC4: KV prewarm probe reduces cold-cache miss rate by >= 70% within the first 3 minutes of cutover
AC5: Dashboard shows cutover scorecard and an automated regression alert if quality/latency degrade beyond configured thresholds
